originality.rationale: Core new claim is the complete center-locus and equality/contact graph of the weighted simplex-generator zonotope. The proof identifies the exact erosion polytope and its affine dimension, plus the special nonuniform unique-center regime and generic high-dimensional freedoms. Closest full-text literature has general scalar radii, inequalities or unweighted Δ-zonotope facets; their scalar consequences are credited, not counted as new. No covering weighted center-space theorem appeared in the targeted actual prior comparisons, subject to acknowledged alternate-terminology risk.
residual_risks: An equivalent older all-weight center-space theorem could exist under metric graph, projection of boxes, or eroded generalized rhombic dodecahedron terminology.
Relevant indexed findings that discuss different center-locus families were compared via indexed summaries rather than their full text; these summaries cannot exclude unseen broader implications.
The scalar radius formulas and PARTITION-style sign characterization are implications of published general zonotope formulas, and are not counted as independently novel.

value.rationale: The full incenter polytope for a natural d+1-generator zonotope family has a sharp, weight-multiplicity-dependent affine dimension. Generic weights yield dimension n−2 with only two centered sphere contacts, but both equal weights and one uniquely smaller weight with all others tied give a unique incenter. The completely different sign-partition control of outer contacts furnishes a motivated inner-versus-outer geometric dichotomy. It is a complete classification rather than a numerical radius substitution.
